clue.text: This 18 is unusually soundly constructed

parts.note: 18 is the gallery of 18-down; the clue describes a gallery built so that a murmur at one side carries clearly round the dome to the other

explanation.surface: Praise for a building whose construction is remarkably solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'solidly' but means acoustically: the famous example is the one in the dome of St Paul's Cathedral, London, where a murmur against the wall is heard across the dome.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of gallery is a round chamber whose curved walls carry faint speech around its circumference.

clue.text: Champagne, madame?

parts.note: a famous champagne house is called after Madame Clicquot, a woman whose husband had died, and the drink is nicknamed after her status

explanation.surface: A waiter offering a lady a glass of champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: Veuve Clicquot champagne means 'Widow Clicquot', so the drink is called 'the Widow'; the madame is that widow.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband has died; also slang for champagne, after Veuve Clicquot.

clue.text: Like Variety cast's nine non-stop performances

indicators.note: variety means diversity, so the letters are given a varied order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive's s counted

explanation.surface: Variety theatre, where the cast give nine continuous shows a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like the music hall, but 'Like Variety' rearranges CAST'S NINE; 'performances' finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means unceasing, carrying on without a break.

clue.text: What's won can't be unwon, more's the pity

definitions.text: What's won can't be unwon, more's the pity

parts.words: What's won can't be unwon, more's the pity
parts.note: a success that cannot be undone even though its cost has ruined the winner

explanation.surface: A rueful twist on the saying that what's done can't be undone.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'what's done can't be undone' is bent to a win one would undo if one could: King Pyrrhus won battles against Rome at ruinous cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph gained at such cost that it amounts to defeat, after King Pyrrhus of Epirus.

clue.text: Gossip — that we're claiming a drink?

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
something we claim belongs to us is ours

explanation.surface: A pub question: is that round of gossip ours to claim?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'rum ours': the drink is the one we are claiming.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumours are unverified stories passed around, which is what gossip is.

clue.text: No Scottish trail coming to light

parts.note: na is the Scots form of no
a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds

explanation.surface: A Scottish hunt reports there is no trail to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, beginning to emerge.

clue.text: Frost giants' father might himself turn frosty

indicators.note: to turn here is to face the other way, so the word for frosty is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: rimy means covered with rime, hoar frost

explanation.surface: A mythic patriarch might share the chill of his icy offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: In Norse myth the primeval giant from whom the frost giants descend is Ymir; written backwards his name gives RIMY, frosty.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology Ymir is the first being, ancestor of the race of frost giants.

clue.text: The real American boxer

definitions.meaning: from the phrase meaning the genuine article
An American boxer of the 1890s, one origin claimed for the phrase

explanation.surface: Calling an American fighter the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: 'the real McCoy' means the genuine thing, and Kid McCoy was a US prizefighter.

clue.text: Journalists who started working in cubby-holes ?

definitions.meaning: those who report, that is present themselves for duty, at their small booths or lodges

explanation.surface: Journalists who began their careers in cramped little offices.
explanation.walkthrough: To report for duty is to arrive and start work, so people who did so are reporters too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: newspaper correspondents, and people who reported for duty to start work.

clue.text: Parts of the Atlantic — not Mare Nostrum

definitions.text: Parts of the Atlantic — not Mare Nostrum

parts.words: Parts of the Atlantic — not Mare Nostrum
parts.note: Mare Nostrum, 'our sea', was the Roman name for the Mediterranean; read 'mare' as a female horse and the male animal gives the start of these zones of the ocean

explanation.surface: Regions of the Atlantic, distinguished from the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin 'mare' (sea) is read as the English mare, so 'not mare' points to the other horse; these calm belts near 30 degrees north and south are not in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm subtropical belts of ocean near thirty degrees latitude, notorious for becalming sailing ships.

clue.text: " Let them cant about Who have characters to lose " (Burns)

definitions.text: " Let them cant about Who have characters to lose " (Burns)

parts.words: " Let them cant about Who have characters to lose " (Burns)
parts.note: a quotation from Robert Burns with a word missing after 'about'; the solver supplies the word for propriety that people with reputations to keep go on about

explanation.surface: A line of Burns mocking those who preach propriety because they have reputations to protect.
explanation.walkthrough: The line, from Burns's The Jolly Beggars, runs 'Let them cant about decorum / Who have characters to lose'; the dash in the printed clue marks the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns's word for the respectable propriety that people with good names lecture others about.

clue.text: Polish white crest

definitions.meaning: a trade name for a white shoe and kit cleaner, a kind of polish
a peak's top covered in snow is a white crest

explanation.surface: Describing a polished white crest, perhaps on a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality here but a product; the second sense is the snow covering a mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain top whitened by snow is its cap; the same word was a trade name for a whitening polish.

clue.text: Where they work with copper in sheets? On the contrary

definitions.text: Where they work with copper in sheets? On the contrary

parts.words: Where they work with copper in sheets? On the contrary
parts.note: reversed, the description becomes a place where they work with sheets in a copper, the large boiler once used for laundry

explanation.surface: A metalworks rolling copper into sheet, which the clue then contradicts.
explanation.walkthrough: A copper was a large metal boiler for heating laundry water; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so the sheets are bedlinen boiled in the copper.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with boilers and tubs where laundry such as bedlinen is done.

clue.text: More modest contestant wins the coconut

definitions.meaning: comparative of an adjective for bashful, retiring
at a fairground coconut stall a player throws, or shies, balls to knock down coconuts

explanation.surface: A bashful competitor carries off the fairground prize.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game: you throw balls to knock coconuts off posts, so one who throws is a shyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: comparative of bashful, and a person who throws at a coconut stall.

clue.text: Money to make one's mark, say, in a post

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to frank a letter is to stamp a mark on it showing postage is paid

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking a letter before it goes in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: FRANK, the postal mark, sounds the same as the French unit of currency; 'in a post' places the franking in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency unit of France, Belgium and Switzerland.

clue.text: Head position for Basil

parts.note: basil the herb is grown in a garden container, and in Keats's poem a lover's head is buried under a pot of basil

explanation.surface: Where a man called Basil should hold his head.
explanation.walkthrough: In Keats's Isabella, or the Pot of Basil, Isabella hides her murdered lover's head in a pot and grows basil over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A container of earth for growing plants, such as a herb like basil.

clue.text: Moon's obscure little sea

indicators.note: to obscure is to confuse or muddy, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Lunar maps name a small dark sea, as the 'seas' of the Moon are called.
explanation.walkthrough: The lunar 'seas' (maria) suggest a lunar-map definition, but 'obscure' rearranges LITTLE SEA; 's is 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon is a natural body orbiting a planet, the general sense of the word.

clue.text: The fashionable Tree girl goes to hospital

parts.note: in means in fashion
a fir is a coniferous tree
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl called Tree, in fashion, is admitted to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a hospital, especially one attached to an institution.

clue.text: Beam a light racing boat

definitions.meaning: a spar projecting from a vessel's side to support a float or rigging
a narrow rowing boat with rowlocks on brackets projecting from the sides

explanation.surface: A ray of light on a sleek racing craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' suggests light, and 'light' then seems to continue it; both are definitions of nautical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a projecting spar on a boat, and a racing shell rowed from rowlocks on such projections.

clue.text: The gods are here regally diverted

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside, so the letters of the word are sent into another order

explanation.surface: Divine beings, royally amused, are present.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods are not deities: in British theatre 'the gods' are the cheapest, highest seats.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the highest balcony with the cheapest seats is nicknamed the gods.

clue.text: Plaything a right old lag might turn to

indicators.note: to turn to is to become, so the letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hardened ex-convict might take up a soft toy.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old lag' is British slang for a habitual criminal; its letters plus R are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a soft stuffed toy made of cloth.

clue.text: Drinks for pets

definitions.meaning: an old word for small sips of liquor
a pet is a fit of sulking; small quarrels or huffs

explanation.surface: Something to drink for one's animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' is not animals but the old noun for a fit of pique, as in 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: little sips of liquor, and petty quarrels or sulks.

clue.text: Worker who backed first channel swimmer each way

indicators.note: backed means sent in reverse, so the swimmer's name is written from end to start

parts.note: Edward Temme was the first man to swim the English Channel in both directions

explanation.surface: A punter who put an each-way bet on the first Channel swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' and 'each way' read as betting terms; in fact 'backed' reverses TEMME, and 'each way' identifies Temme, first to swim the Channel from both coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: An emmet is an old and dialect name for an ant, the classic worker insect.

clue.text: Intended for inclusion in some anthology

indicators.note: the answer is included within the letters of the following words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A poem was meant to go into an anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past tense of mean, to have in mind as a purpose.

clue.text: Give well-mixed glue a stir to make these binding

definitions.note: ligatures are bindings; the plural answer is the things that do the binding

indicators.note: something well mixed has been stirred thoroughly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Glue-making instructions: stir it well so it sets and binds.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is plural, picked up by 'these' in 'to make these binding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligatures are cords or threads used to tie and bind, as in surgery.

clue.text: Girl from the south with a spot-on throw

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
a die is a spotted cube you throw

explanation.surface: A Southern girl who throws with perfect accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot-on' seems to mean accurate, but the throw is a die, which has spots on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadie is a girl's name, a pet form of Sarah.

clue.text: Was it plain sailing in such a schooner ?

definitions.text: Was it plain sailing in such a schooner ?

parts.words: Was it plain sailing in such a schooner ?
parts.note: a covered settlers' wagon was nicknamed after a ship and crossed the grassland plains of North America

explanation.surface: Asking whether a voyage aboard a certain sailing ship was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain sailing' means easy going, but here the plain is grassland: the covered wagons of American pioneers were called after a schooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie schooner was the canvas-covered wagon that carried settlers across the plains.

clue.text: Skilled workman of long service

parts.note: an experienced worker who has been at the job for years, described plainly

explanation.surface: A veteran craftsman with many years on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a veteran, someone with long experience and skill.

clue.text: Picture 18

parts.note: 18 is the gallery of 18-down; the clue asks for a gallery of pictures

explanation.definitionFit: The Tate in London is a famous art gallery holding British and modern paintings.

clue.text: Lost before close of play in time of revolution-it will make copy

indicators.note: in places the run of lost letters inside the word for a period of revolution

parts.note: a cycle is the time taken by one complete revolution

indicators.note: before puts the word lost ahead of the final letter that follows it
the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A game lost near its end during a revolution, followed by a copying machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of revolution' suggests a political uprising, but it is a period of rotation. The device defined was an early stencil duplicator for office copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclostyle was an early duplicating device that printed copies from a cut stencil.
